tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the man asked to do this evening?

options.A: Say a few words to thank the speaker.
options.B: Introduce the speaker to the audience.
options.C: Give a lecture on the history of the town.
options.D: Host a talk on how to give a good speech.

questions.cn: 今晚请男士做什么？

optionsCn.B: 向听众介绍演讲人。
optionsCn.C: 做一场关于小镇历史的讲座。
optionsCn.D: 主持一场关于如何做好演讲的讲座。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man?

options.A: He was the founder of the local history society.
options.B: He has worked with Miss Bligh for 20 years.
options.C: He has published a book on public speaking.
options.D: He joined the local history society when young.

questions.cn: 关于男士，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他是当地历史学会的创始人。
optionsCn.B: 他和布莱小姐共事了 20 年。
optionsCn.C: 他出版了一本关于演讲的书。
optionsCn.D: 他年轻时加入了当地历史学会。

questions.stem: What does the man say about Miss Bly?

options.A: She was obviously better at talking than writing.
options.B: She had a good knowledge of the town's history.
options.C: Her speech was so funny as to amuse the audience.
options.D: Her ancestors came to the town in the 18th century.

questions.cn: 关于布莱小姐，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 她显然更擅长讲话而非写作。
optionsCn.B: 她对这座小镇的历史很了解。
optionsCn.C: 她的演讲太滑稽，把听众逗乐了。
optionsCn.D: 她的祖先在 18 世纪来到这座小镇。

questions.stem: What does the man say about the first time he gave a speech of thanks?

options.A: He read exactly what was written in his notes.
options.B: He kept forgetting what he was going to say.
options.C: He made an embarrassing remark.
options.D: He was too nervous to speak up.

questions.cn: 关于他第一次致答谢辞，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 他老是忘记要说什么。
optionsCn.C: 他说了一句令人尴尬的话。
optionsCn.D: 他紧张得说不出话。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: F: You're going to give a short speech of thanks for the speaker this evening, aren't you, Bill?
lines.cn: F：比尔，今晚你要为演讲人致一段简短的答谢辞，对吧？

lines.t: M: Yes.
lines.cn: M：是的。

lines.t: F: You don't sound very enthusiastic.
lines.cn: F：你听起来不太热情啊。

lines.t: F: It's not that bad, is it?
lines.cn: F：也没那么糟吧？

lines.t: M: No, I don't mind really, but I can never forget the first speech of thanks I did.
lines.cn: M：不，其实我并不介意，但我永远忘不了我第一次致答谢辞的情景。

lines.t: F: Why, what happened?
lines.cn: F：怎么了？发生什么事了？

lines.t: M: Well, I was in my early twenties.
lines.cn: M：嗯，那时我二十出头。

lines.t: M: I had joined the local history society.
lines.cn: M：我加入了当地的历史学会。

lines.t: F: Yes.
lines.cn: F：嗯。

lines.t: M: Anyway, I went along to a lecture by a Miss Bly.
lines.cn: M：总之，我去听了一位布莱小姐的讲座。

lines.t: F: Oh, do go on.
lines.cn: F：哦，继续说。

lines.t: M: She was going to talk, with slides, about our town in the 18th century.
lines.cn: M：她要配合幻灯片，讲我们这座小镇 18 世纪的历史。

lines.t: M: She had just published a book on the subject, which was reckoned to be quite good.
lines.cn: M：她刚就这个主题出了一本书，评价还相当不错。

lines.t: M: So, I went along.
lines.cn: M：所以我就去了。

lines.t: M: When I arrived, the secretary asked me if I could give the speech of thanks.
lines.cn: M：我到的时候，秘书问我能不能致答谢辞。

lines.t: M: Rather stupidly, I said yes.
lines.cn: M：我挺傻地答应了。

lines.t: F: We've all done it.
lines.cn: F：这种事我们都干过。

lines.t: M: Anyway, from that point on, I was scared.
lines.cn: M：总之，从那一刻起，我就慌了。

lines.t: M: What should I say?
lines.cn: M：我该说些什么呢？

lines.t: M: I decided to make notes during the lecture and refer to interesting parts and thank her on behalf of the society.
lines.cn: M：我决定在讲座中做笔记，提到那些有意思的内容，并代表学会向她致谢。

lines.t: M: In fact, by the time Miss Bly stood up to talk, I was feeling much better.
lines.cn: M：事实上，等到布莱小姐站起来开讲时，我已经感觉好多了。

lines.t: M: But she was so nervous that she kept forgetting what to say.
lines.cn: M：但她太紧张了，老是忘记要说什么。

lines.t: M: And she spoke almost in a whisper.
lines.cn: M：而且她说话几乎像耳语。

lines.t: M: People at the back kept calling out, we can't hear.
lines.cn: M：后面的人不断喊：我们听不见。

lines.t: M: It was embarrassing.
lines.cn: M：真是尴尬。

lines.t: F: I can imagine it.
lines.cn: F：我能想象。

lines.t: M: At least the slides were good.
lines.cn: M：至少幻灯片还不错。

lines.t: M: That is, until the bulb in the projector blew, and she had to finish the talk with no illustrations.
lines.cn: M：直到投影仪的灯泡烧了，她只好在没有图像的情况下把讲座讲完。

lines.t: F: So what did you say in your speech of thanks?
lines.cn: F：那你的答谢辞是怎么说的？

lines.t: M: What can you say?
lines.cn: M：你还能说什么呢？

lines.t: M: You have to be polite.
lines.cn: M：总得客气点。

lines.t: M: I mentioned the interesting facts, referred to the excellent slides, and then finished up by saying, we'd all like to thank Miss Bly for blowing us her slides.
lines.cn: M：我提到了那些有趣的内容，称赞了出色的幻灯片，最后说：我们都想感谢布莱小姐把幻灯片给“吹”了。

lines.t: F: Oh no!
lines.cn: F：哦，不会吧！

lines.t: M: I felt terrible.
lines.cn: M：我难受极了。

lines.t: M: I tried to apologize, not very successfully.
lines.cn: M：我试着道歉，但不太成功。

lines.t: F: And the speech of thanks this evening?
lines.cn: F：那今晚的答谢辞呢？

lines.t: M: I'll write down exactly what I'm going to say, and read it carefully.
lines.cn: M：我会把要说的话一字一句写下来，然后仔细照着念。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the woman think the man should know?

options.A: What their retailers demand.
options.B: What their rivals are doing.
options.C: How they are going to beat their rivals.
options.D: How dramatically the market is changing.

questions.cn: 女士认为男士应该知道什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们的零售商有什么要求。
optionsCn.B: 他们的竞争对手在做什么。
optionsCn.C: 他们要怎么打败对手。
optionsCn.D: 市场变化有多剧烈。

questions.stem: What does the woman think of Barrett's company?

options.A: They should be taken seriously.
options.B: They are rapidly catching up.
options.C: How they are going to beat their rivals.
options.D: How dramatically the market is changing.

questions.cn: 女士怎么看巴雷特的公司？

optionsCn.B: 他们正在迅速赶上。
optionsCn.C: 他们要怎么打败对手。
optionsCn.D: 市场变化有多剧烈。

questions.stem: What did the woman say about the letter from the tax revenue office?

options.A: She had given it to Tom.
options.B: It simply made her go frantic.
options.C: She had not seen it yet.
options.D: It was not much of a big concern.

questions.cn: 关于税务局的那封信，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 它只是让她慌了神。
optionsCn.C: 她还没看到那封信。
optionsCn.D: 那件事没什么大不了的。

questions.stem: What is the man thinking of doing?

options.A: Restructuring the whole company.
options.B: Employing more forwarding agents.
options.C: Promoting cooperation with Jayal Motors.
options.D: Exporting their motorbikes to Indonesia.

questions.cn: 男士打算做什么？

optionsCn.B: 雇用更多货运代理。
optionsCn.C: 推动与杰尔汽车公司的合作。
optionsCn.D: 把他们的摩托车出口到印度尼西亚。

lines.t: Conversation two.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: F: Another cup of tea, Paul?
lines.cn: F：保罗，再来一杯茶吗？

lines.t: M: No thanks.
lines.cn: M：不用了，谢谢。

lines.t: M: Well, what's new, Laurie?
lines.cn: M：那么，有什么新情况吗，劳丽？

lines.t: F: Nothing dramatic, but there's something you should know about.
lines.cn: F：没什么大事，但有件事你应该知道。

lines.t: M: What's that?
lines.cn: M：什么事？

lines.t: F: Well, our rivals are offering extended credit terms to some of the retailers in the area.
lines.cn: F：嗯，我们的竞争对手正在向本地区的一些零售商提供延期付款条件。

lines.t: M: Oh?
lines.cn: M：哦？

lines.t: M: Which rival's this?
lines.cn: M：是哪家对手？

lines.t: M: We only have two.
lines.cn: M：我们只有两家对手。

lines.t: F: Barrett's company.
lines.cn: F：巴雷特的公司。

lines.t: M: Oh, them.
lines.cn: M：哦，是他们。

lines.t: M: Well, they're hardly a threat.
lines.cn: M：嗯，他们算不上什么威胁。

lines.t: F: I know they're smaller than us, but we can't afford to ignore them.
lines.cn: F：我知道他们比我们小，但我们不能忽视他们。

lines.t: M: Yes, you're right, Laurie.
lines.cn: M：是的，你说得对，劳丽。

lines.t: M: But I don't like extended credit.
lines.cn: M：但我不喜欢延期付款。

lines.t: M: It ties up cash we could put to better use elsewhere.
lines.cn: M：它占用了我们本可以用在别处更划算的资金。

lines.t: M: But I'll look into it on Monday.
lines.cn: M：不过周一我会去研究一下这件事。

lines.t: F: Yes, and there's something else.
lines.cn: F：好，还有别的事。

lines.t: M: Don't tell me.
lines.cn: M：别告诉我……

lines.t: M: The letter from the tax revenue office?
lines.cn: M：税务局的那封信？

lines.t: F: Right.
lines.cn: F：对。

lines.t: F: How did you know?
lines.cn: F：你怎么知道的？

lines.t: M: Tara told me.
lines.cn: M：塔拉告诉我的。

lines.t: M: What's the problem?
lines.cn: M：有什么问题？

lines.t: F: Well, Tom got this letter late yesterday and then went frantic trying to find copies of last year's accounts.
lines.cn: F：嗯，汤姆昨天很晚才收到这封信，然后就疯了似的找去年账目的副本。

lines.t: M: Did he find them?
lines.cn: M：他找到了吗？

lines.t: F: No, and he was away before I could get hold of the letter.
lines.cn: F：没有，而且我还没来得及拿到那封信，他就走了。

lines.t: M: How about a drive down to the office now?
lines.cn: M：现在开车去办公室一趟怎么样？

lines.t: M: And we'll see if everything's alright.
lines.cn: M：我们去看看是不是一切正常。

lines.t: F: There's another reason why I wanted to chat with you before Monday.
lines.cn: F：我想在周一之前和你聊聊，还有另一个原因。

lines.t: M: I thought as much.
lines.cn: M：我早就猜到了。

lines.t: M: Well, go on, surprise me.
lines.cn: M：说吧，给我个惊喜。

lines.t: M: How about selling that new motorcycle of yours in Indonesia?
lines.cn: M：把你那款新摩托车卖到印度尼西亚去，怎么样？

lines.t: F: What?
lines.cn: F：什么？

lines.t: F: You mean export?
lines.cn: F：你是说出口？

lines.t: F: Paul, I think you've been away too long.
lines.cn: F：保罗，我看你在外面待得太久了。

lines.t: F: This is Jail Motors.
lines.cn: F：这里是杰尔汽车公司。

lines.t: F: We've never sold a bike abroad.
lines.cn: F：我们从来没把摩托车卖到国外过。

lines.t: M: Don't worry, Laurie.
lines.cn: M：别担心，劳丽。

lines.t: M: I'm not crazy.
lines.cn: M：我没疯。

lines.t: M: I've been studying the possibility and I think we should give it a go.
lines.cn: M：我一直在研究这种可能性，我觉得我们应该试一试。

lines.t: F: It's not as easy as that though, is it?
lines.cn: F：可事情没那么简单，是不是？

lines.t: F: We'd have to reorganise the whole company.
lines.cn: F：我们得把整个公司重新组织一遍。

lines.t: M: Don't be silly.
lines.cn: M：别说傻话。

lines.t: M: I don't intend starting next week.
lines.cn: M：我又不打算下周就开始。

lines.t: M: We'll have to plan it properly.
lines.cn: M：我们得好好规划。

lines.t: M: And of course there'll be a few problems.
lines.cn: M：当然会有一些难题。

lines.t: F: A few problems?
lines.cn: F：一些难题？

lines.t: F: I can see hundreds.
lines.cn: F：我能看到上百个。

lines.t: F: For one thing, transport.
lines.cn: F：首先就是运输。

lines.t: F: I have enough trouble delivering bikes to shops only 40 miles away, never mind 5,000 miles.
lines.cn: F：光是给 40 英里外的商店送车我就够头疼了，更别说 5000 英里。

lines.t: M: That's what forwarding agents are for.
lines.cn: M：那正是货运代理存在的意义。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the report released this month?

options.A: It makes claims in conflict with the existing research.
options.B: It focuses on the link between bedtime and nutrition.
options.C: It cautions against the overuse of coffee and alcohol.
options.D: It shows that "night owls" work much less efficiently.

questions.cn: 关于本月发布的这份报告，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它的结论与现有研究相矛盾。
optionsCn.B: 它关注就寝时间与营养之间的联系。
optionsCn.C: 它告诫人们不要过量饮用咖啡和酒精。
optionsCn.D: 它表明“夜猫子”的工作效率低得多。

questions.stem: What does the study from the University of California, Berkeley, find about teens who go to bed late?

options.A: They pay greater attention to food choice.
options.B: They tend to achieve less than their peers.
options.C: They run a higher risk of gaining weight.
options.D: They stand a greater chance to fall sick.

questions.cn: 加州大学伯克利分校的研究对晚睡的青少年发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们更注重食物的选择。
optionsCn.B: 他们的成就往往低于同龄人。
optionsCn.C: 他们发胖的风险更高。
optionsCn.D: 他们生病的可能性更大。

questions.stem: What should night owls do to reduce their consumption of unhealthy food?

options.A: Get up late.
options.B: Sleep 8 hours a day.
options.C: Exercise more.
options.D: Go to bed earlier.

questions.cn: 夜猫子应该怎么做才能减少不健康食品的摄入？

optionsCn.B: 每天睡 8 小时。
optionsCn.C: 多锻炼。
optionsCn.D: 早点上床睡觉。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: A report on sleep and nutrition released this month found that people who consistently went to bed earlier than 11 p.
lines.cn: 本月发布的一份关于睡眠与营养的报告发现，总是在晚上 11 点

lines.t: m.
lines.cn: 之前

lines.t: took in fewer calories and ate more healthy food.
lines.cn: 上床睡觉的人摄入的热量更少，吃的食物也更健康。

lines.t: In contrast, night owls who go to bed between 11 p.
lines.cn: 相比之下，那些在晚上 11 点

lines.t: m.
lines.cn: 至凌晨

lines.t: and 3 a.
lines.cn: 3 点

lines.t: m.
lines.cn: 之间入睡的“夜猫子”

lines.t: tend to consume more coffee, alcohol, refined sugars and processed meats than early risers.
lines.cn: 往往比早起的人摄入更多咖啡、酒精、精制糖和加工肉类。

lines.t: This report corresponds with the existing scientific literature on bedtime and wellness.
lines.cn: 这份报告与现有的关于就寝时间与健康的科学文献相吻合。

lines.t: The relationship between getting more sleep and making better food choices is well documented.
lines.cn: 睡得更多与选择更健康食物之间的关系已有充分的研究记录。

lines.t: A study published last year in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition found that people who sleep more tend to eat less unhealthy food than their peers who don't get as much rest.
lines.cn: 去年发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上的一项研究发现，睡眠较多的人比休息不足的同龄人吃的不健康食品更少。

lines.t: And a 2015 study from the University of California, Berkeley, found that teens who go to bed late are more likely to gain weight over a five-year period.
lines.cn: 加州大学伯克利分校 2015 年的一项研究发现，睡得晚的青少年在五年内更容易发胖。

lines.t: As a group, night owl types tend to eat less healthy food and take in more calories overall than early risers.
lines.cn: 总体而言，夜猫子型的人吃的不健康食品更多，摄入的总热量也比早起者多。

lines.t: The later one goes to bed, the more calories one records the next day.
lines.cn: 上床越晚，第二天摄入的热量就越多。

lines.t: It is as yet a challenge to explain the cause-and-effect relationship between sleep and nutrition.
lines.cn: 目前要解释睡眠与营养之间的因果关系仍是个难题。

lines.t: There may be a third factor that impacts both of them, or the relationship could be reversed, that is, people who eat less fall asleep earlier.
lines.cn: 可能存在同时影响两者的第三种因素，或者这种关系是反向的，也就是说，吃得少的人睡得更早。

lines.t: Still, if late sleepers want to lose a few pounds, they can go to bed earlier than they usually do, thereby reducing their chances of taking snacks before bedtime.
lines.cn: 不过，如果晚睡的人想减掉几磅体重，可以比平时更早上床睡觉，从而减少睡前进食零食的机会。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why has the Oscars ceremony been criticized?

options.A: All of the acting nominees are white.
options.B: It has got too much publicity on TV.
options.C: It is prejudiced against foreign films.
options.D: Only 7% of the nominees are female.

questions.cn: 奥斯卡颁奖礼为什么受到批评？

optionsCn.A: 所有表演类提名者都是白人。
optionsCn.B: 它在电视上获得了过多曝光。
optionsCn.C: 它对外国影片有偏见。
optionsCn.D: 只有 7% 的提名者是女性。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the research?

options.A: 22 percent of movie directors were people of color.
options.B: Half of the TV programs were ethnically balanced.
options.C: Only one-fifth of TV shows had black characters.
options.D: Only 3.4 percent of film directors were women.

questions.cn: 我们从这项研究中了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 22% 的电影导演是有色人种。
optionsCn.B: 一半的电视节目族裔构成是平衡的。
optionsCn.C: 只有五分之一的电视节目有黑人角色。
optionsCn.D: 只有 3.4% 的电影导演是女性。

questions.stem: Who are regarded as largely invisible on TV shows?

options.A: Non-white males.
options.B: Program creators.
options.C: Females of color over 40.
options.D: Asian speaking characters.

questions.cn: 在电视节目中被视为基本隐形的是谁？

optionsCn.B: 节目创作者。
optionsCn.C: 40 岁以上的有色人种女性。
optionsCn.D: 说亚洲语言的亚裔角色。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about Hispanics?

options.A: They constitute 17% of Hollywood movie characters.
options.B: They are most underrepresented across TV and film.
options.C: They contribute little to the U.S. film industry.
options.D: They account for 8.5% of the U.S. population.

questions.cn: 关于拉美裔，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们占好莱坞电影角色的 17%。
optionsCn.B: 他们在电视和电影中的代表性最为不足。
optionsCn.C: 他们对美国电影业贡献很小。
optionsCn.D: 他们占美国人口的 8.5%。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: Researchers have found not just a diversity problem in Hollywood, but actually an inclusion crisis.
lines.cn: 研究人员发现，好莱坞不仅存在多元化问题，实际上还面临一场包容性危机。

lines.t: With less than a week before an Oscars ceremony that has already been criticised for an all-white list of acting nominees, a study shows the film industry does worse than television.
lines.cn: 距离已因表演类提名清一色为白人而受到批评的奥斯卡颁奖礼不到一周，一项研究显示电影业的表现比电视业更糟。

lines.t: Just 3.
lines.cn: 只有 3.

lines.t: 4% of film directors were female, and only 7% of films had a cast whose balance of race and ethnicity reflected the country's diversity.
lines.cn: 4% 的电影导演是女性，只有 7% 的影片其演员阵容的种族与族裔构成能反映全国的多样性。

lines.t: When researchers looked at all TV shows, they also found that women of colour over 40 were regarded as largely invisible, and just 22 % of TV series creators were female.
lines.cn: 研究人员在考察所有电视节目时还发现，40 岁以上的有色人种女性基本被视为隐形，而电视剧创作者中只有 22% 是女性。

lines.t: Overall, the study found half the films and TV shows had no Asian-speaking characters, and more than one-fifth of them had no black characters with dialogue.
lines.cn: 总体而言，研究发现有一半的电影和电视节目没有说亚洲语言的亚裔角色，超过五分之一完全没有有台词的黑人角色。

lines.t: The film industry still functions as a straight, white boys' club.
lines.cn: 电影业依然像一个异性恋白人男性的俱乐部那样运作。

lines.t: When looking at how women are depicted, the study found female characters were four times more likely to be shown in sexy clothing, and nearly four times as likely to be referred to as physically attractive.
lines.cn: 在考察女性形象的呈现方式时，研究发现女性角色穿着性感服装出镜的可能性是男性的四倍，被形容为外貌迷人的可能性也接近四倍。

lines.t: But their results also indicated films and TV shows with women or people of colour in the important jobs behind the scenes – director, producer or writer – tended to have better diversity numbers.
lines.cn: 但结果也表明，在导演、制片人或编剧等幕后重要岗位上有女性或有色人种的电影和电视节目，其多元化数据往往更好。

lines.t: Across TV and film, the under-representation of non-white characters falls mostly on Hispanics.
lines.cn: 在电视和电影中，非白人角色代表性不足的问题主要集中在拉美裔身上。

lines.t: Among more than 10,000 characters, proportions of white, black and Asian characters came close to US population figures.
lines.cn: 在一万多个角色中，白人、黑人和亚裔角色的比例接近美国的人口数据。

lines.t: But Hispanics were just 5.
lines.cn: 但拉美裔只占角色的 5.

lines.t: 8% of characters, despite being about 17% of the US population.
lines.cn: 8%，尽管他们约占美国人口的 17%。

questions.stem: What life insurance should a single person buy according to the speaker?

options.A: One that can provide for emergency needs.
options.B: One that can pay for their medical expenses.
options.C: One that covers their debts and burial expenses.
options.D: One that ensures a healthy life for their later years.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，单身人士应该购买什么样的人寿保险？

optionsCn.A: 能应对紧急需要的保险。
optionsCn.B: 能支付医疗费用的保险。
optionsCn.C: 能覆盖其债务和丧葬费用的保险。
optionsCn.D: 能确保晚年健康生活的保险。

questions.stem: What should people do as their family increases in size?

options.A: Purchase insurance for their children.
options.B: Save sufficient money for a rainy day.
options.C: Buy a home with a small down payment.
options.D: Add more insurance on the breadwinner.

questions.cn: 家庭规模扩大时，人们应该怎么做？

optionsCn.B: 存足够的钱以备不时之需。
optionsCn.C: 以少量首付买房。
optionsCn.D: 为养家者增加保险。

questions.stem: When should one change their life insurance?

options.A: When their children grow up and leave home.
options.B: When they have saved enough for retirement.
options.C: When their family moves to a different place.
options.D: When they have found better-paying jobs.

questions.cn: 人们应该在什么时候调整自己的人寿保险？

optionsCn.B: 当他们存够退休金时。
optionsCn.C: 当家庭搬到别的地方时。
optionsCn.D: 当他们找到薪水更高的工作时。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: When purchasing life insurance, there are many important factors to consider.
lines.cn: 购买人寿保险时，有许多重要因素需要考虑。

lines.t: One should buy the policies that give the most protection at the least cost, insure the right family members and consider the family's financial needs.
lines.cn: 人们应当购买以最低成本提供最大保障的保单，为合适的家庭成员投保，并考虑家庭的财务需求。

lines.t: It is important to buy the insurance from companies that are financially sound and that are represented by honest, well-trained agents.
lines.cn: 重要的是，要向财务稳健、且有诚实且训练有素的代理人代表的公司购买保险。

lines.t: At various stages in a person's life, different kinds of life insurance are needed for particular situations.
lines.cn: 在人生的不同阶段，特定的情况需要不同种类的人寿保险。

lines.t: Jerry is single and has no dependents.
lines.cn: 杰里单身，没有需要供养的人。

lines.t: Probably the only life insurance he needs is enough to cover his debts and burial expenses.
lines.cn: 他大概只需要足够偿付债务和丧葬费用的保险。

lines.t: Insurance can be purchased at a lower rate during the young years, but by buying while young, the premiums are paid in for a longer period of time.
lines.cn: 年轻时购买保险费率更低，但年轻时投保，缴纳保费的期限也会更长。

lines.t: In the end, the amount paid for premiums is about the same.
lines.cn: 最终，所缴纳的保费总额大致相当。

lines.t: A person shouldn't buy insurance protection that really isn't necessary.
lines.cn: 人不应该购买其实并不必要的保险保障。

lines.t: Suppose that Jerry marries Jeanette, who is a college graduate and is working.
lines.cn: 假设杰里和珍妮特结婚了，她大学毕业，正在工作。

lines.t: Perhaps enough insurance would be needed to cover their debts and burial expenses.
lines.cn: 或许需要足够的保险来偿付他们的债务和丧葬费用。

lines.t: Now, Jeanette has quit work and their first child is on the way.
lines.cn: 现在，珍妮特辞去了工作，他们的第一个孩子即将出生。

lines.t: They have purchased a home with a small down payment and a 30-year mortgage.
lines.cn: 他们以少量首付和 30 年期按揭买了一套房子。

lines.t: The situation regarding life insurance takes on a different look.
lines.cn: 人寿保险的情况就变得不同了。

lines.t: There are dependents who need financial protection.
lines.cn: 有了需要经济保障的被抚养人。

lines.t: How much insurance is needed?
lines.cn: 需要多少保险？

lines.t: As the family increases in size, it is essential to add more insurance on the breadwinner to protect the dependents.
lines.cn: 随着家庭规模扩大，必须为养家者增加保险，以保障被抚养人。

lines.t: When the children are young and depend upon the family for financial needs, families with modest incomes have difficulty providing enough life insurance to protect the mother and the children.
lines.cn: 孩子年幼、经济上依赖家庭时，收入不高的家庭很难提供足够的人寿保险来保障母亲和孩子。

lines.t: Families with modest incomes should insure the breadwinner or breadwinners first.
lines.cn: 收入不高的家庭应首先为养家者投保。

lines.t: When considering the amount of insurance for the mother with dependent children, substitute child care is a need that should be planned for until the children can care for themselves.
lines.cn: 在考虑需抚养孩子的母亲的保险额度时，替代性托育是一项应提前规划的需求，直到孩子能够照顾自己。

lines.t: The death of a small child would have no effect upon the income of the family.
lines.cn: 幼儿的死亡不会影响家庭的收入。

lines.t: Perhaps a policy to meet funeral expenses would be sufficient for the young child, although most people do not take out insurance on their young children.
lines.cn: 对幼儿来说，一份足以支付丧葬费用的保单也许就够了，尽管大多数人并不会为年幼的孩子投保。

lines.t: As the children become financially independent of the family, the emphasis on family financial security will shift from protection to saving for the retirement years.
lines.cn: 当孩子在经济上不再依赖家庭时，家庭财务保障的重点将从保障转向为退休岁月储蓄。

lines.t: Every family situation is different, but it is important that each family give adequate thought to planning its financial future.
lines.cn: 每个家庭的情况都不同，但重要的是每个家庭都要充分考虑规划自己的财务未来。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about stereotypes?

options.A: They do more harm than good.
options.B: They have often been ignored.
options.C: They do not help build friendship.
options.D: They may not always be negative.

questions.cn: 关于刻板印象，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 它们常常被忽视。
optionsCn.C: 它们无助于建立友谊。
optionsCn.D: 它们并不总是负面的。

questions.stem: What leads to the bias of stereotypes?

options.A: Biased sources of information.
options.B: Ignorance of cultural differences.
options.C: Misinterpretation of Shakespeare.
options.D: Tendency to jump to conclusions.

questions.cn: 是什么导致刻板印象出现偏差？

optionsCn.B: 对文化差异的无知。
optionsCn.C: 对莎士比亚的误解。
optionsCn.D: 急于下结论的倾向。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is a problem with stereotypes?

options.A: They are hard to dismiss once attached to a certain group.
options.B: They may have a negative impact on people they apply to.
options.C: They persist even when circumstances have changed.
options.D: They are often applied to minorities and ethnic people.

questions.cn: 讲话者说刻板印象的一个问题是什么？

optionsCn.A: 一旦与某个群体挂钩就很难消除。
optionsCn.B: 它们可能对被套用的人产生负面影响。
optionsCn.C: 即使情况已经改变，它们依然存在。
optionsCn.D: 它们常常被用于少数族裔和族群。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Stereotype may sound like a bad word, but there's nothing bad about it.
lines.cn: “刻板印象”听起来可能像个贬义词，但它本身并没有什么不好。

lines.t: For one thing, stereotypes are often accurate.
lines.cn: 首先，刻板印象往往是准确的。

lines.t: When you ask people about their concept of stereotypes, they get it pretty much right.
lines.cn: 当你问人们对刻板印象的理解时，他们的理解大体上是正确的。

lines.t: Also, stereotypes are often positive, particularly of groups that we ourselves belong to.
lines.cn: 此外，刻板印象常常是正面的，尤其是对于我们自己所属于的群体。

lines.t: Some of the statistical generalisations may be positive, as some groups have reputations for being smart, for being loyal, for being brave, for all sorts of things that are not at all negative.
lines.cn: 有些统计上的概括可能是正面的，因为有些群体以聪明、忠诚、勇敢等著称，这些都不是负面的东西。

lines.t: And so there's nothing inherently wrong about stereotypes.
lines.cn: 所以刻板印象本身并没有什么内在的错误。

lines.t: But there are problems with stereotypes.
lines.cn: 但刻板印象也存在问题。

lines.t: For one thing, they are reliable insofar as they are based on unbiased samples.
lines.cn: 首先，只有当它们建立在无偏差的样本之上时才是可靠的。

lines.t: But a lot of the information we get about human groups is through biased sources, like how they are represented in the media.
lines.cn: 但我们获得的关于人类群体的许多信息都来自有偏差的渠道，比如媒体对他们的呈现方式。

lines.t: And if these sources don't give you an accurate depiction, your stereotype won't be accurate.
lines.cn: 如果这些渠道没有给你准确的描述，你的刻板印象就不会准确。

lines.t: For example, many Jews have been troubled by Shakespeare's depiction of Shylock.
lines.cn: 例如，许多犹太人为莎士比亚笔下的夏洛克形象感到困扰。

lines.t: If the only Jew you know is Shakespeare's Shylock, it's going to be a very bad impression.
lines.cn: 如果你认识的唯一的犹太人就是莎士比亚笔下的夏洛克，那会是很糟的印象。

lines.t: So one problem with stereotypes is while we're good at drawing conclusions from them, often our information isn't reliable.
lines.cn: 所以刻板印象的一个问题是：虽然我们擅长由此得出结论，但我们掌握的信息往往并不可靠。

lines.t: A second problem is that stereotypes, regardless of whether or not they're accurate, can have a negative effect on the people that they apply to.
lines.cn: 第二个问题是，刻板印象无论准确与否，都可能对被套用的人产生负面影响。

lines.t: And this is what psychologist Claude Steele described as stereotype threat.
lines.cn: 这就是心理学家克劳德·斯蒂尔所说的“刻板印象威胁”。

lines.t: He has a vivid example of this.
lines.cn: 他有一个生动的例子。

lines.t: Here's how to make African Americans do worse on a math test.
lines.cn: 以下就是如何让非裔美国人在数学考试中表现更差的办法。

lines.t: You have the test and you put on the test that they have to identify their race.
lines.cn: 你把试卷发下去，并在试卷上要求他们填写自己的种族。

lines.t: The very act of acknowledging that they're African American when given a test ignites in them thoughts of their own stereotype, which is negative regarding academics, and that makes them do worse.
lines.cn: 在考试时承认自己是非裔美国人这一举动本身，就点燃了他们对自己刻板印象的联想——那种在学业上的负面印象——从而使他们表现更差。

lines.t: Want to know how to make a woman do worse on a math test?
lines.cn: 想知道怎么让女性在数学考试中表现更差吗？

lines.t: Same thing.
lines.cn: 同样的办法。

lines.t: Get her to write down her sex.
lines.cn: 让她写下自己的性别。

lines.t: One recent study found a sort of clever twist on this.
lines.cn: 最近一项研究发现了这方面一个巧妙的转折。

lines.t: When Asian American women are given a test and they're asked to mark down their race, they do better than they would otherwise do.
lines.cn: 当亚裔美国女性参加考试并被要求填写种族时，她们的表现比不填时要好。

lines.t: They're reminded of a positive stereotype that boosts their morale.
lines.cn: 她们被提醒起一种正面的刻板印象，从而提振了士气。

lines.t: You ask them, on the other hand, to mark down their sex, they do worse because they're reminded of a negative stereotype.
lines.cn: 相反，如果你让她们写下性别，她们的表现就会变差，因为她们被提醒起一种负面的刻板印象。

lines.t: That's an example of how stereotypes have a potentially damaging effect on people.
lines.cn: 这就是刻板印象可能对人造成伤害的一个例子。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What did one recent study find about stereotypes?

options.A: They impact people more or less in the same way.
options.B: Some people are more sensitive to them than others.
options.C: A positive stereotype may help one achieve better results.
options.D: A negative stereotype sticks while a positive one does not.

questions.cn: 最近一项研究对刻板印象发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们对人的影响大体相同。
optionsCn.B: 有些人比其他人对它们更敏感。
optionsCn.C: 正面的刻板印象可能有助于取得更好的成绩。
optionsCn.D: 负面刻板印象会留存，正面则不会。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say you should do when you have an adverse reaction?

options.A: Use some over-the-counter medicine instead.
options.B: Quit taking the medicine immediately.
options.C: Take some drug to relieve the side effects.
options.D: Ask your pharmacist to explain why it occurs.

questions.cn: 讲话者说出现不良反应时你应该怎么做？

optionsCn.B: 立即停止服用该药。
optionsCn.C: 吃些药来缓解副作用。
optionsCn.D: 请药剂师解释为什么会发生。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about alcohol drinking?

options.A: It may help patients fall asleep.
options.B: It may lead to mental problems.
options.C: It may cause serious harm to one's liver.
options.D: It may increase the effect of certain drugs.

questions.cn: 关于饮酒，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 它可能导致精神问题。
optionsCn.C: 它可能严重损害肝脏。
optionsCn.D: 它可能增强某些药物的作用。

questions.stem: What does the speaker call on parents to do at the end of the talk?

options.A: Tell their children to treat medicines with respect.
options.B: Keep medicines out of the reach of their children.
options.C: Make sure their children use quality medicines.
options.D: Ask their children to use legitimate medicines.

questions.cn: 讲话者在结尾呼吁父母做什么？

optionsCn.A: 告诉孩子要认真谨慎地对待药物。
optionsCn.B: 把药物放在孩子够不到的地方。
optionsCn.C: 确保孩子使用优质药物。
optionsCn.D: 要求孩子使用合法药物。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Sometimes, when you take a common drug, you may have a side effect.
lines.cn: 有时，服用一种常见药物时，你可能会出现副作用。

lines.t: That is, the drug may cause some effect other than its intended one.
lines.cn: 也就是说，药物可能产生并非其预期的效果。

lines.t: When these side effects occur, they are called adverse reactions.
lines.cn: 这些副作用发生时，被称为不良反应。

lines.t: Whenever you have an adverse reaction, you should stop taking the drug right away.
lines.cn: 一旦出现不良反应，你就应该立即停止服用该药。

lines.t: Ask your pharmacist whether he can suggest a drug that will relieve the symptoms, but that will not cause the adverse reaction.
lines.cn: 问问药剂师能否推荐一种既能缓解症状、又不会引起该不良反应的药物。

lines.t: If an adverse reaction to a drug is serious, consult your doctor for advice at once.
lines.cn: 如果药物不良反应严重，应立即咨询医生。

lines.t: Drugs that are safe in the dosage stated on the label may be very dangerous in large doses.
lines.cn: 按标签标明剂量服用是安全的药物，大剂量服用可能非常危险。

lines.t: For example, aspirin is seldom thought of as dangerous, but there are many reports of accidental poisoning of young children who take too many aspirin pills, as well as the possible development of Reye's syndrome in children with the flu.
lines.cn: 例如，阿司匹林很少被认为危险，但已有很多报道称幼儿因服用过多阿司匹林片而意外中毒，以及患流感的儿童可能出现瑞氏综合征。

lines.t: In adults, excessive use of some pain-killing drugs may cause severe kidney damage.
lines.cn: 在成人中，过量使用某些止痛药可能导致严重的肾损伤。

lines.t: Some drugs for relief of stomach upsets, when taken in excess, can perhaps cause serious digestive problems.
lines.cn: 一些缓解胃部不适的药物若过量服用，可能引起严重的消化问题。

lines.t: You should never use any over-the-counter drug on a regular, continued basis or in large quantities, except on your doctor's advice.
lines.cn: 除非遵医嘱，否则绝不应长期、持续或大量使用任何非处方药。

lines.t: You could be suffering from a serious illness that needs a doctor's care.
lines.cn: 你可能正患有一种需要医生诊治的严重疾病。

lines.t: Each drug you take not only acts on the body, but may also alter the effect of any other drug you are taking.
lines.cn: 你服用的每一种药物不仅作用于身体，还可能改变你正在服用的其他任何药物的效果。

lines.t: Sometimes this can cause dangerous or even fatal reactions.
lines.cn: 有时这会引发危险甚至致命的反应。

lines.t: For example, aspirin increases the blood-thinning effects of drugs given to patients with heart disease.
lines.cn: 例如，阿司匹林会增强给心脏病患者所用药物的抗凝血作用。

lines.t: Therefore, a patient who has been taking such a drug may risk bleeding if he or she uses aspirin for a headache.
lines.cn: 因此，正在服用这类药物的病人如果为了治头痛而服用阿司匹林，就可能面临出血风险。

lines.t: Before using several drugs together, you should ask your doctor and follow his advice.
lines.cn: 同时使用几种药物之前，应咨询医生并遵从医嘱。

lines.t: Your pharmacist can tell you whether certain drugs can safely be taken together.
lines.cn: 药剂师可以告诉你某些药物能否安全地一起服用。

lines.t: Alcohol may increase the effect of a drug.
lines.cn: 酒精可能增强药物的作用。

lines.t: Sleeping pills combine with alcohol to produce a sleepy feeling.
lines.cn: 安眠药与酒精共同作用会产生困倦感。

lines.t: When taking any drug, you should ask your doctor whether drinking alcohol could be dangerous in combination with the medicine.
lines.cn: 服用任何药物时，都应该问医生饮酒与这种药同用是否危险。

lines.t: Experts believe there is a relationship between adult abuse of legitimate medicines and the drug culture that has swept our country.
lines.cn: 专家认为，成年人滥用合法药物与席卷我们国家的药物文化之间存在关联。

lines.t: You can do your share to reduce the chances that your children will become part of the drug culture by treating all medicines with respect.
lines.cn: 认真谨慎地对待所有药物，你就能尽自己的一份力，减少孩子卷入药物文化的可能。

lines.t: Always let your children know that medicines and drugs should not be used carelessly.
lines.cn: 始终让孩子明白，药物不应被随意使用。
